ca_configuration.title: Configure Certificate Authority
ca_configuration.description_upload_or_create: In this step you can either upload or create a new certificate authority.
ca_configuration.description_provision: The certificate authority will provision and manage certificates for your Data Nodes more easily.
ca_configuration.reusing_certificates: If your existing cluster uses certificates, by default these will get replaced with the {{productName}} CA and automatically generated certificates during provisioning of the data nodes in the next step. If you want to include your own CA, you can upload an existing certificate. Please see <docsLink>{{productName}} Data Node - Getting Started</docsLink> for more information.

ca_create.description: Click on the “Create CA” button to quickly create a new certificate authority for your {{productName}} Data Nodes.

ca_upload.single_file: Please upload only a single file.
ca_upload.explanation: Here you can upload your existing CA. You need to upload a single file containing both private key (encrypted or unencrypted), the CA certificate as well as any intermediate certificates. The file can be in PEM or in PKCS#12 format. If your private key is encrypted, you also need to supply its password.
ca_upload.dropzone: Drag CA here or click to select file

state_help.question: How does my cluster change state during the rolling upgrade?
state_help.red: RED - if you are using indices with no replication and upgrade the node hosting the shards of these indices, the cluster will go to a red state and no data will be ingested into or searchable from these indices.
state_help.yellow: YELLOW - after starting the upgrade of a node, shard allocation will be set to no replication to allow OpenSearch to use only the available shards.
state_help.green: After a node has been upgraded and you click on <emphasis>Confirm Upgrade</emphasis>, shard replication will be re-enabled and all shards that were unavailable due to the node being upgraded will be re-allocated and the cluster will return to a GREEN state.

shard_replication_help.start: After you click on <emphasis><bold>Start Upgrade Process</bold></emphasis> of a node, shard allocation will be set to no replication to allow OpenSearch to use only the available shards.
shard_replication_help.confirm: After a node has been upgraded and you click on <emphasis><bold>Confirm Upgrade</bold></emphasis>, shard replication will be re-enabled and all shards that were unavailable due to the node being upgraded will be re-allocated.

upgrade_method.cluster_restart_description: When using the cluster restart method, you will upgrade all Data Nodes at once. During this time, messages will be buffered in the journal and processed as the Data Node cluster comes back online, leading to no data loss provided your journal size is configured for the message volume which is expected during the Data Node downtime.
upgrade_method.cluster_restart_less_than_three: If you are running a Data Node cluster with less than three nodes, the cluster restart method is the only method available.
upgrade_method.cluster_restart_three_or_more: If you are running a Data Node cluster with three or more nodes, you can choose to use the cluster restart method after consideration of your journal size and your message throughput.
upgrade_method.rolling_upgrade_description: Rolling upgrades can be performed on a running Data Node cluster only with <bold>three or more nodes</bold>, with virtually no downtime.
upgrade_method.rolling_upgrade_process: Data Nodes are individually stopped and upgraded in place. Alternatively, Data Nodes can be stopped and replaced, one at a time, by hosts running the new version. During this process you can continue to index and query data in your cluster.

rolling.title: Start OpenSearch rolling upgrade?
rolling.alert_title: This restarts every Data Node, one at a time
rolling.each_node_with_versions_one: Each of your {{count}} Data Nodes will be upgraded and restarted one at a time to move its embedded OpenSearch from {{currentVersion}} to {{targetVersion}}.
rolling.each_node_with_versions_other: Each of your {{count}} Data Nodes will be upgraded and restarted one at a time to move its embedded OpenSearch from {{currentVersion}} to {{targetVersion}}.
rolling.each_node_one: Each of your {{count}} Data Nodes will be upgraded and restarted one at a time to move its embedded OpenSearch to the target version.
rolling.each_node_other: Each of your {{count}} Data Nodes will be upgraded and restarted one at a time to move its embedded OpenSearch to the target version.
rolling.shard_allocation: Shard allocation is paused during each restart, so the cluster stays available — but indexing and search may be briefly degraded while a node leaves and rejoins.
rolling.wait_for_green: After each node the upgrade waits for the cluster to return to green before continuing. If that takes too long it pauses and waits for you to resume.
rolling.healthy_cluster: Make sure the cluster is healthy (green) before proceeding.

full.title: Restart Data Nodes' OpenSearch?
full.alert_title: Fewer than 3 Data Nodes — this is a full restart, not a rolling one
full.restart_together_with_versions_one: With fewer than 3 Data Nodes, OpenSearch can't stay available by restarting one node at a time. All your Data Nodes restart together to move OpenSearch from {{currentVersion}} to {{targetVersion}}, so the storage backend is unavailable until they finish — search and indexing are interrupted.
full.restart_together_with_versions_other: With fewer than 3 Data Nodes, OpenSearch can't stay available by restarting one node at a time. All your Data Nodes restart together to move OpenSearch from {{currentVersion}} to {{targetVersion}}, so the storage backend is unavailable until they finish — search and indexing are interrupted.
full.restart_together_one: With fewer than 3 Data Nodes, OpenSearch can't stay available by restarting one node at a time. All your Data Nodes restart together to move OpenSearch to the target version, so the storage backend is unavailable until they finish — search and indexing are interrupted.
full.restart_together_other: With fewer than 3 Data Nodes, OpenSearch can't stay available by restarting one node at a time. All your Data Nodes restart together to move OpenSearch to the target version, so the storage backend is unavailable until they finish — search and indexing are interrupted.
full.journal: While OpenSearch is down, incoming messages pile up in the disk journal on each {{productName}} node. If the outage outlasts the journal's size or age limit, ingestion stalls and messages can be dropped — only proceed if the journal has enough headroom for the expected downtime.
full.tolerate_downtime: Proceed only if you can tolerate the downtime.
